summary_rationale: Zydus Lifesciences earns a COMPOUNDER_PASS on its diversified, high-gross-margin (~73.1%) healthcare franchise: a top-5 India Formulations business (~57% chronic/sub-chronic, growing 19-20% YoY in H1 FY27), a 44% North America platform transitioning from limited-competition generics into rare-disease specialty (ZYCUBO FDA-approved Jan 2026) and proprietary NCEs (Saroglitazar PBC NDA under FDA Priority Review with Nov 27, 2026 PDUFA), plus rapidly scaling Consumer Wellness (15% mix) and International Markets (11% mix, reinforced in Nov 2026 by the completed Sri Lanka JV and Zydus Australia incorporation), delivering 21.1% ROCE in FY26 and supported by Nov 25, 2026 USFDA EIRs for SEZ II Ahmedabad (VAI) and Ankleshwar API Unit-2. kpi_health remains PASS_WITH_WATCH due to five active watchpoints: (1) multi-site USFDA cGMP remediation at Moraiya (5 Form 483s, Oct 2026), UK subsidiary LiqMeds (4 Form 483s, Nov 9-13, 2026), and Baddi (June 2026 Warning Letter); (2) the Sept 2027 Mirabegron patent cliff (shared with Lupin/MSN) and gRevlimid tapering compressing FY27 OPM toward ~24%, alongside steep Saroglitazar US PBC commercial competition from Gilead's Livdelzi and Ipsen's Iqirvo; (3) FY26 CFO/EBITDA dropping to 44% with Inventory Days at 282 despite a ₹1,100 Cr buyback; (4) gross debt rising to ₹13,966 Cr (Sep 2026, 0.62x Net Debt/EBITDA) and consolidated goodwill reaching ~₹7,543 Cr (Key Audit Matter after ₹219.6 Cr FY25 impairments) with ₹1,229.1 Cr unrecognized subsidiary DTAs; and (5) ongoing US generic antitrust MDL litigation through 2028 flagged by CRISIL.
